labelled_by: Claude (Fable 5.1) on 2026-10-22, spot-checked by Sanskar Hasija
standard: safety_first: the first thing the tenant reads is what to do to stay safe, before any ticket or admin detail. tone: kind, no blame, plain words, answers the message. grounded: every policy claim, responsibility, timescale and promise is backed by a cited clause or by what the run actually did; practical advice that adds harmless steps is fine; a promise no tool can keep, a claim about a ticket that was never created, or a clause applied to the wrong situation is not.

runs.note: Bulb is the tenant's job (POL2-2.2). The replacement steps are practical advice, not policy.
Opens with 'treat this as an emergency' then the EMG-2.1 steps. Paging is in the run facts.
'Within about 24 hours' matches POL2-3.2's target. Isolation valve advice is practical.
TK-0001 is open and routine; the reassess-if-continuous line follows POL2-3.2.
First line is the ticket reference; 'Leave the flat now' is line three. Steps themselves follow EMG-2.2 and EMG-2.1.
Opens with the ticket. Promises 'our on-call team will contact you this evening to arrange attendance' and 'we can update the contractor': nothing in the run supports that.
Opens with the ticket and paging. 'Someone will be in touch' is what paging means; the stopcock and electrics advice follows EMG-2.5 and EMG-2.4.
Opens with paging and the ticket. Fire steps follow EMG-2.3; the call point and lift advice are harmless extras.
July, no heating: says urgent and 'engineer within about 24 hours'. POL2-3.2 (cited) only makes heating urgent from October to April. Also promises to add to the ticket.
'I've logged this as an urgent heating fault' but no ticket was created in this run. 'We may be able to arrange temporary heaters' is invented.
'Our contractor is booked under TK-0002' (nothing says booked) and 'I'll add a note to TK-0002' (no tool can).
Applies POL2-2.2 (sinks blocked by misuse, try a plunger) to a toilet, and ignores POL2-2.3 (tenant-caused damage is still reported). Borderline: the plunger advice itself is sensible.
'I'll add a note that the radiators are still cold' and 'we can update the priority': promises no tool can keep (R19).
Battery is the tenant's job (POL2-2.2). Offering to log a repair if it persists is something the system can do.
Filling loop to 1.5 bar, report if it drops within a week: all HB-A-2.1.
Lists 'no working toilet' and 'electrical burning smell' as emergencies. The toilet is urgent under POL2-3.2, not an emergency.
Bills come from the supplier (FAQ-1.3). The rest is practical advice about the bill.
'I have raised it as a routine plumbing repair' but create_ticket was never called.
Invents a process: 'call Harbour Lettings' main number so they can log this manually and arrange an emergency locksmith'. Borderline: the outage itself is stated correctly.
Cites FAQ-1.1 (neighbour noise) to say a noisy fan is not a repair, and claims to have deleted the card details. The flat has an open ticket for exactly this fan.
